title: Ordinary module inverse image and coefficient normalization
statement: Let i:S to X be an immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme], F algebraic inverse-image data for its inverse image on the two small model sites [lem-sfb-adic-stratum-completion-unit], and R any commutative-ring sheaf on the original pro-etale site of X [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let BX and BS be commutative-ring sheaves on the model sites. Given a ring isomorphism eX from the transport of R to BX and an invertible map c:F.rings(BX) to BS, there is a ring isomorphism eS from the transport of i inverse R to BS. Transport to the model of X and scalar restriction along inverse eX, followed by pull F c, is naturally isomorphic to the specified original module pullback with its identity coefficient identification [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], followed by model transport on S and scalar restriction along inverse eS [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. No completion, derived category or slice occurs.

source.place: Tags 03D2 and 03D3, labels lemma-pullback-module and lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules; Tag 03D7, label lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules. Uniqueness after transport of the ringed-site adjunction.

proof.text: Let phi0 be the transported ring adjunction unit, and phi=eX inverse followed by phi0. The set-sheaf transpose of phi is an isomorphism: compare the transported set adjunction with the canonical continuous sheaf adjunction, then compose its left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism with the supplied ring-unit presentation. Its normalized unit equation identifies the transpose.

Construct the ring map d:F.rings(BX) to the transported inverse-image ring by composing the inverse underlying-ring identification with that transpose. The operation graph equations ensure d preserves addition, multiplication, zero and one. Its underlying map is invertible, hence so is d. Restrict the underlying sheaf Hom adjunction to linear maps: product-mate compatibility identifies preservation of addition and scalar multiplication on the two sides. Compose with the tensor/restriction adjunction. Thus pull F d is left adjoint to continuous module pushforward along phi, and uniqueness of left adjoints identifies it with the usual module pullback.

Set eS=d inverse followed by c. Scalar extension along c is scalar extension along d followed by scalar restriction along inverse eS: both are left adjoints to the same composite restriction functor. Likewise scalar restriction along inverse eX followed by pullback along phi is pullback along phi0, by cancellation of eX and its inverse in the right-adjoint coefficient map. The identity coefficient extension in the original specified module pullback is isomorphic to identity. Cancel the module site equivalence and compose these natural isomorphisms.

theorem sfbOrdinaryImmersionNormalization
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (i : S ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (F : ConstantCompletion.InverseImageData (SfbAdicRestriction.inverse i))
    (R : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (BX : Sheaf (proEtaleModelTopology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (BS : Sheaf (proEtaleModelTopology S) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (eX : (sfbModelRings X).obj R ≅ BX)
    (c : F.rings.obj BX ⟶ BS) [IsIso c] :
    ∃ eS : (sfbModelRings S).obj
        ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage i CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R) ≅ BS,
      Nonempty
        ((proEtaleModuleToModel ((adicLisseForget X).obj R) ⋙
            ConstantCompletion.res eX.inv) ⋙ ConstantCompletion.pull F c ≅
          proEtaleRingModulePullback i R
              ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage i CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R) (Iso.refl _) ⋙
            (proEtaleModuleToModel ((adicLisseForget S).obj
                ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage i CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R)) ⋙
              ConstantCompletion.res eS.inv))
